page: Microsoft Azure EC64ads_cc_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor runs at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and is supported by 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 2458 GB, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU hardware is present on this server configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in multi-core processing and memory operations. The server achieves a top-tier rating in PassMark memory score and strong performance in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, PassMark database operations, and Redis SET operations, which reached 62.79 million operations per second. However, there are distinct performance tradeoffs. While cached memory bandwidth is strong at 4162.65 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths drop to average levels of 121.12 GB/sec and 62.68 GB/sec respectively. Additionally, while text generation for small LLM models is strong, text generation for large 70B LLM models is weak, registering at 2.74 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the EC64ads_cc_v5 offers a dense allocation of memory and local storage relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads requiring high memory capacity without the premium cost of GPU accelerators. The combination of 512 GB of RAM, 2458 GB of local storage, and strong multi-core performance makes this server highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale Redis deployments, multi-threaded data decompression, and general memory-optimized enterprise workloads.
